name: CalSTRS
rationale: Most governance-advanced public pension per its own peer research; GenAI policy, cost-benefit analysis, and prioritized pipeline of scalable use cases (25 scoped) in place. Explicitly following a governance-first, deploy-later approach — preconditions for scaling met, but not yet firm-wide production.

GenAI policy, cost-benefit analysis, and pipeline of scalable use cases presented to board; staff AI bootcamp set for September

name: CalPERS
rationale: Board-level AI education only. Jan 2026 board education day featured a Jefferies macro briefing ('AI: What We Need to Know') covering AI fundamentals, economics, and geopolitics — AI as an investment/market topic, not internal use. No public GenAI policy, use-case pipeline, pilot, or deployment as of early 2026; roughly a stage behind CalSTRS.

name: NBIM (Norges Bank Investment Management)
rationale: Most AI-advanced LP publicly. ~50% of 700 staff build their own Claude-based tools in production for screening, ESG/risk monitoring across 7,000 holdings, and meeting prep; 3-year firm-wide push with AI teams, ambassadors, and mandatory training. Stops short of embedded: AI cannot make autonomous investment decisions — human oversight is non-negotiable.

events.event: Publishes 'Responsible AI' position paper (board accountability, transparency, risk management)
~50% of 700 staff building their own Claude tools; roadmap toward supervised-autonomous agents
